Ossified

OSS-uh-fyed · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ossified is become rigid and resistant to change.

Decades without reform had left the agency's procedures completely ossified.

Worked Example

Once a flexible startup, the company's decision-making had become so ossified that even small changes required five layers of approval.

Ossified describes a system, structure, or set of rules that has become so fixed and unchanging over time that it can no longer adapt.

How Ossified Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rigid

rigid: fixed and unable to bend or change

fossilized

fossilized: hardened into a fixed, unchanging form

Antonyms

flexible

flexible: able to adapt and change easily

dynamic

dynamic: constantly changing and active

How Strong Is It? — outdated → ossified → fossilized

outdated vs. ossified

outdated vs. ossified: Something outdated is simply old; it could still be updated fairly easily.

fossilized vs. ossified

fossilized vs. ossified: Something fossilized has hardened into permanent stone, an even more extreme rigidity than merely ossified.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of ossified.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — oss

root — oss: bone (Latin (os, ossis))

suffix — -ify

suffix — -ify: to make, to turn into (Latin (-ificare))

suffix — -ed

suffix — -ed: having undergone the process of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: oss ("bone") + -ify ("to make into") + -ed = turned into bone -- hardened and fixed.

Use the root in a new word: ossuary

Use the root in a new word: ossuary: The same root gives us "ossuary," a chamber or container used to hold the bones of the dead.
